messages:
alex (Sales): Quick heads-up — Acme wants POC access to a Dedicated endpoint. Their network team needs our egress IPs to allowlist. @maya can you confirm options and lead time?

maya (SE): Hey — yes. Two fast paths for POC: ephemeral NAT IPs for a short window (fast, free), or request static egress IPs bound to the Dedicated pool (slower, small monthly fee). Ephemeral may change on pool failover.

raj (Acme NetEng): Hi all — for compliance we prefer fixed IPs but procurement will slow things down. For the POC we can open a 48h window if you give us IPs. Also: will the hostname/TLS change? We need SNI for outbound TLS inspection.

maya (SE): Good call. For Dedicated endpoints the hostname is customer-specific (eg: acme-dedicated.redwood.ai) and we manage TLS certs by default. If you need client-managed certs or mTLS, we can discuss Private deployment.

olivia (Security): If they require fixed egress IPs for production, we do offer a "Reserved Egress IP" add-on (enterprise). That adds an approval step and a monthly fee. For the POC, a 48h allowlist is acceptable from a security POV provided audit logs are kept.

raj (Acme NetEng): OK POC timeline: we'd like to test tomorrow morning 10:00 PDT. Can you give two IPs and a simple curl example to smoke test? Also confirm whether health/failover will flip IPs mid-test.

maya (SE): Temp egress IPs (ephemeral) we can assign right away; they may change on pool failover but that's unlikely during short window. Current ephemeral IPs we have available for acme-poc: 34.120.45.23/32, 34.120.45.24/32 (subject to change until confirmed). Please allow outbound to port 443 to those IPs.

maya (SE): Example firewall rule (allowlist):

```
# allow HTTPS to Redwood Dedicated POC
allow from any to 34.120.45.23/32 port 443 proto tcp
allow from any to 34.120.45.24/32 port 443 proto tcp
```

maya (SE): Curl smoke test (use scoped API key we'll send off-channel):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer POC-XXXX-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://acme-dedicated.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-jax-1-20b","input":"ping"}'
```

alex (Sales): Pricing note — Reserved Egress IPs add ~+$500/mo for a small pool for POC (one-time pro rata may apply). If Acme wants guaranteed static IPs for production we'll put that in the quote.

raj (Acme NetEng): For the POC we accept the 48h ephemeral window. Please confirm the exact two IPs by EOD and send the scoped API key via secure channel. Also, do you expose metrics or syslog endpoints that we need to allow?

maya (SE): Confirmed: we'll lock the two IPs after we provision the pool and DM the API key. We do push metrics to a Redwood endpoint by default but for POC we can disable pushes — we can also provide a scrapping endpoint if you prefer to pull. If you want logs forwarded to your syslog, we'll need the destination IP/port and agreement to TLS.

deploy-bot: Automated: Dedicated pool created for acme-poc-2026 (pool-id: dp-9f3c).

olivia (Security): Quick checklist for us to sign off after the test: 1) confirm API key scope is limited to generation only, 2) ensure audit logging enabled, 3) confirm ephemeral IPs were used and rotation timeline.

raj (Acme NetEng): Will open the firewall for the two IPs for 48h starting 10:00 PDT tomorrow. We'll run the smoke test and share results.

maya (SE): Great — next steps Ilya-style summary: 1) SE to DM scoped API key + curl (today) 2) Sales to confirm cost/quote note on Reserved Egress (if they elevate) 3) Acme to open firewall 34.120.45.23/24 for 48h starting 10:00 PDT 4) Security to confirm post-test checklist. Ping me if anything blocks. :thumbsup:

alex (Sales): I'll update the deal thread and procurement contact. Thanks everyone.

raj (Acme NetEng): Thanks — will report back after the test.
